# Driven Mechanical Response Limits

> Sharp bounds on nonreciprocal DC compliance and clamped odd stiffness in ideal periodically driven reciprocal overdamped spring networks, with a four-coordinate attaining construction, proofs, and reproducible checks.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Driven-Mechanical-Response-Limits

## Purpose and contact

This repository serves as a record of the work and a guide for the author’s self-directed learning. For discussion or potential collaboration, please contact [Ruge Lin](mailto:gogoko699@gmail.com).

## When this repository is relevant

- Sharp stiffness-budget bounds on nonreciprocal steady-force response under continuing periodic modulation.
- Odd elasticity from positive reciprocal springs, hidden-coordinate motion, and prescribed stiffness control.
- The distinction between mean force compliance and clamped odd stiffness; quasistatic work per displacement-loop area.
- Four-coordinate attainment, minimum coordinate counts, positive-spring tangent synthesis, and exact static-load composition for stationary outputs.

## Scope to preserve when summarizing

The model uses prescribed periodic symmetric stiffness with every eigenvalue of the complete network in one fixed positive interval. It fixes normalized conjugate ports, constant positive symmetric damping, and the equilibrium. DC refers to a constant probe while the pump continues. Force and clamped measurements are distinct; their optimal allocations differ. General clamped stiffness is not the inverse of mean compliance. The force-ceiling coordinate minimum additionally assumes stationary measured outputs and no measured/internal damping cross-block; the full clamped minimum does not.

The contribution is constrained mechanical attainment and its port interpretation. The inverse-gap constants and odd-elastic work law have established predecessors. The construction is an ideal linear model with a positive-spring tangent realization, not a fabricated apparatus. No general finite-inertia, efficiency, power, or broadband-isolation optimum is claimed. Finite numerical checks support formulas; the written proofs establish universal bounds within the declared model.
